text: Lithium burns with a strongly red-tinged flame, and in pure oxygen the flame is even stronger.
Lithium starts to burn when it is heated in air.
Melted lithium catches fire quite easily and is then hard to put out.
Lithium oxide is corrosive and can injure the skin, the eyes and the breathing passages.
Gold is one of a few metals, along with silver and platinum, that do not react with oxygen.
Oxygen mostly does not react with gold.
Lithium oxide is a white powder with no smell.
Lithium oxide is used to soak up carbon dioxide gas.
Lithium oxide is used to make special kinds of glass and ceramics.
